# Real Chrome ClientHello records, with the JA4 that FoxIO's own
# implementation produces for each.
#
# Source: https://github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4, pcap/tls-sni.pcapng
# (sha256 1c869a87ae758f390765672e5ba9ed96cc075e2ee131e94efb29fe98e4d417e1),
# expected values from python/test/testdata/tls-sni.pcapng.json.
#
# JA4 (TLS client fingerprinting) is BSD-3-Clause, per LICENSE-JA4 in that
# repository:
#
#   Copyright (c) 2026 FoxIO. All rights reserved.
#   Redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without
#   modification, are permitted provided that the following conditions are
#   met: redistributions of source code must retain the above copyright
#   notice, this list of conditions and the following disclaimer.
#   THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED BY THE COPYRIGHT HOLDERS AND CONTRIBUTORS
#   "AS IS" AND ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTIES ARE DISCLAIMED.
#
# The hello bytes were lifted straight out of the TCP stream with gopacket,
# not with this package, so the fixture cannot inherit a bug from the parser
# it exists to check.
#
# Format: <tcp source port> <expected JA4> <TLS record, hex>

# ALPN h2, 16 extensions. The common case.
50112 t13d1516h2_8daaf6152771_e5627efa2ab1 

# ALPN http/1.1, which JA4 collapses to h1: proves the first-and-last rule.
50122 t13d1516h1_8daaf6152771_e5627efa2ab1 

# No ALPN at all, encoded 00, and 14 extensions rather than 16.
50123 t13d151400_8daaf6152771_de4a06bb82e3 

# 17 extensions, so a different sorted-extension hash from every other row.
50153 t13d1517h1_8daaf6152771_6cdcb247c39b
